item.title: Anthony Joshua silences Prenga with brutal second-round knockout
item.description: Anthony Joshua overcame a dramatic first-round scare before knocking out Kristian Prenga in the second round of their heavyweight clash at the Jeddah Superdome in Saudi Arabia. The British former world champion secured the victory at the official time of 2 minutes and 43 seconds of round two in the DAZN pay-per-view main event this morning.
item.content:encoded:
Anthony Joshua overcame a dramatic first-round scare before knocking out Kristian Prenga in the second round of their heavyweight clash at the Jeddah Superdome in Saudi Arabia.

The British former world champion secured the victory at the official time of 2 minutes and 43 seconds of round two in the DAZN pay-per-view main event this morning.

Joshua found himself in trouble early as Prenga came out aggressively and landed a powerful right uppercut that appeared to stun the heavyweight. The Albanian fighter continued to apply pressure, driving Joshua back towards the ropes and forcing him to touch the canvas, resulting in a counted knockdown.

Despite the early setback, Joshua remained composed and responded in the second round. He regained control with his jab before setting up a powerful right hand that ended Prenga’s challenge and secured the knockout victory.

The win improves Joshua’s record to 29 victories, four defeats and 26 knockouts, while Prenga drops to 20-2 after entering the bout with an impressive record of 20 wins and 20 knockouts.

There were no judges’ scorecards required as Joshua stopped the contest before the end of the second round.

The victory keeps Joshua’s plans for a highly anticipated showdown with Tyson Fury later this year alive.

However, for a brief period in Jeddah, Prenga threatened to derail those plans with a fearless opening attack.

Joshua’s experience and power ultimately proved decisive, allowing him to recover from the early danger and secure another statement win in the heavyweight division. Source: DAZN/Middleeasy

item.title: Lomary Secondary thrash MGM High 18-0 in Raluve U18 Southern Zone final
Grammar defeat Nasinu 25-19 in U19 Southern Zone Deans final
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 25/07/2026 The Suva Grammar School Under-19 rugby side came from 12-3 down at halftime to defeat Nasinu Secondary School 25-19 in the Vodafone Deans Southern Zone Secondary Schools Rugby Union final at Grammar Ground this afternoon.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 25/07/2026

The Suva Grammar School Under-19 rugby side came from 12-3 down at halftime to defeat Nasinu Secondary School 25-19 in the Vodafone Deans Southern Zone Secondary Schools Rugby Union final at Grammar Ground this afternoon.

Nasinu started strongly, scoring two tries in the first half to take a 12-3 lead at halftime. However, Grammar regrouped in the second half and managed to break through Nasinu's defence.

Grammar scored three second-half tries through hard work and perseverance to complete the comeback victory.

In other results, MGM High School beat Suva Grammar School 20-10 to claim the Under-14 title, Suva Grammar edged rivals Marist Brothers High School 24-17 in the Under-15 final, MGM High defeated Nasinu Secondary School 19-12 in the Under-16 final, and Suva Grammar edged Gospel High School 23-22 in the Under-17 final.

item.title: Fiji women's pairs target Kenya clash after Wales defeat at Commonwealth Championships
item.description: Litia Tikoisuva and Losalini Tukai will be hoping to keep Fiji's semi-final hopes alive when they take on Kenya after going down 2-0 to Wales in their second-round clash in Glasgow. The experienced Fijian pair went down 0-8, 3-5 to Amy Williams and Lauren Gowen of Wales at the SEC Centre today.
item.content:encoded:
Litia Tikoisuva and Losalini Tukai will be hoping to keep Fiji's semi-final hopes alive when they take on Kenya after going down 2-0 to Wales in their second-round clash in Glasgow.

The experienced Fijian pair went down 0-8, 3-5 to Amy Williams and Lauren Gowen of Wales at the SEC Centre today.

Fiji struggled in the opening set, failing to register a single shot as Wales raced to a 3-0 lead after two ends and maintained control throughout the set.

A crucial fifth end saw Fiji's first four bowls finish close to the jack before Wales' fifth bowl broke up the head to claim the full count and seal the set 8-0.

The Fijian duo responded with a much-improved performance in the second set.

They claimed the opening end to lead 1-0 before Wales levelled with two shots. Fiji then regained the advantage with two shots at the third end to move 3-2 ahead.

However, Wales levelled the scores at 3-3 in the fourth end before finishing strongly, picking up two shots in the final end to secure the set 5-3 and complete the straight-sets victory.

Despite the defeat, Tikoisuva and Tukai remain optimistic heading into tomorrow's third-round match.

Fiji now have one win and one loss in Section C after opening their campaign with a victory over Botswana and remain in contention for a place in the semi-finals.

They will take on Kenya at 3pm local time tomorrow on Rink 3 , with Kenya still searching for their first win after losing their opening two matches.
